Long story, I'll give a TLDR at the end. Just need to rant, and ask your opinions on this issue.

At the beginning of August, I transitioned out of the military with the intent to start school that September for an ECE Program. Seeking a part time job, I saw a listing for a part time Electro/Mech Maintenance Technician Trainee at a VERY large company. Applied, and I got the interview.

During the interview, they disclosed that as part of the program, I would receive a $5000 "bonus" per year ($15000 total) for being part of the "pilot/test program". Currently they are doing 20 of these "pilot/test programs" in the nation, to be done in conjunction with a full time enrollment in an accredited college program. It is a 3 year position, and at the end of the 3 years, given good enough performance review, they would hire you on. Please note, that this $5000 a year was NOT on the original job listing, however it was something that the Maintenance Manager, and the Hiring Manager repeatedly stressed.

I was offered an official letter, where the Maintenance Manager once again mentioned this $5000 bonus for enrolling in the program. I had several other part time jobs lined up (With MUCH higher pay), as well as the possibility of simply collecting unemployment during college. With an extra $15000 waiving in my face, I accepted the offer. Maintenance Manager said that we would file the paperwork for the bonus at the end of the fiscal year.

Ask boss about paperwork a few weeks ago. Says he will track down what forms we will specifically need to fill out as part of the programs bonus. Couple days later he approaches me, and says even though he has it in writing that it's a $5000 flat rate paid to me, HR is saying that it cant work like that, and I will have to fall under Tuition Reimbursement, and they can just adjust the cap to the 5k per year. No where during the interview, or signing of the hiring paperwork, was it disclosed that I would be ineligible for tuition reimbursement on account of receiving other forms of financial aid. They said that part wouldn't apply to me, b/c i fall under the "pilot program".

Okay. Cool.

Fill out paperwork for Tuition Reimbursement. Clearly stated in there "Tuition payments will not be reimbursed if employee is receiving financial aid that already meets the cost of tuition for the accredited institution." Which, by me collecting the MGIB, and pulling in Veterans Tuition Award (State pays the state school, I keep the money from the MGIB), my financial aid exceeds the limit of tuition by A LOT.

I submitted the paperwork to HR today, and am honestly going to be livid if they deny it.

I took the job on account of the $5000 yearly bonus being waived in my face during the interview. I feel wronged, and misled. Part of me feels like I'm being discriminated against because of me being a Veteran. Were I not a Veteran, and in this same program, I would receive the money, as I qualify for no other forms of financial aid. And then I keep getting dicked around by the company as to what is happening with this now null and void tuition reimbursement shenanigans! I would have probably opted on one of the other offers if it wasn't disclosed to me like this during the interview.

What are your guys thoughts? I need some advice here. If I don't get the 5k a year as was disclosed to me, do I have grounds to sue over this? Should I even consider it?

TLDR: Hiring Manager told me I get a 5k yearly bonus for a part time college program, and they keep reneging and changing the story. Now I am more than likely not eligible.
Do you guys think I have a valid cause to file a lawsuit against my employer over this?
If all else fails, burn it to the ground. Make sure that the employer loses potential business and employees, until they come clean.

From the sound of it, you should cut your ties and losses with this company and go apply at the other places that offered you more money, if you are still able. I'm not an attorney but it definitely sounds like your basically SOL here. That whole tuition reimbursement clause they put in there along with your MGIB aid (which is well deserved), fucks you. The way that your aid is coming through is making it easy peasy for this company to fuck over servicemen, so if you are going to speak to attorney, one should probably research if and/or how many other servicemen have had the same issue with this company. If it turns out that this business has a trend/habit of using similar (and provable) tactics, then you would have a great case.

All of that will cost you a lot of time and money, so I say work for them until you line up a better job.

Daily Devotional

November 3

36 He that believeth on the Son hath everlasting life: and he that believeth not the Son shall not see life; but the wrath of God abideth on him. (John 3:36 KJV)

Everlasting life, or eternal life, is not just something we will have in the future sometime, but the second you are born again, with the spirit of Jesus, by believing on Jesus and making Him your Lord and Savior (Romans 10:9-10), you have everlasting life. The scriptures tell us that everlasting life is not just living forever, which we will do, but it is to know God and Jesus in an intimate way (John 17:3), and is for us now in this life and forever after, as long as we obey Jesus (Hebrews 5:9). So many Christians miss the point of Salvation, as they just think it is being saved from hell, but it is meant to be much more than that. It includes healing, deliverance and prosperity in this life right now, and then getting to live forever with God and Jesus in eternity.

All those that turn down the free gift of salvation that is offered by believing on Jesus, will be judged and the wrath of God will be poured out on them (Revelations 16). Why anyone would want to have the wrath of God instead of the love of God, I don’t understand. It certainly seems like a no-brainer to choose life instead of death, but as the bible says, we have the choice, and can choose life or death (Deuteronomy 30:19). God gave mankind a free will and He will protect our free will even if we choose to go to hell instead of heaven. Thank you Jesus for bringing us the ability to have relationship with the Father once again, and giving us all the Grace gifts that you have provided. Praise God for His mercy, and His Gifts of healing, deliverance, prosperity, fruit of the Spirit, etc. Thank you Father!

Devotional by Pastor Joe W. Green, www.Infinite-Faith.com
